  "what_the_study_did": "The study developed and validated the ZeGlobalTox assay, an integrated platform using zebrafish larvae to assess cardio-, neuro-, and hepatotoxicity of compounds.",

    {
      "quote": "We will show that by using ZeGlobaltox, a high toxicity predictivity is achieved—specificity (89%), sensitivity (68%), and accuracy (78%).",
      "topic": "Predictivity Metrics"
    },
    {
      "quote": "These results reinforce the validation of zebrafish as a suitable model for pre-mammalian studies to reduce and/or replace mammalian vertebrate usage, experimental time, and cost during the process of drug discovery and development.",
      "topic": "Zebrafish Validation"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Results obtained through the ZeGlobalTox assay show high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy values when we compare the zebrafish experimental data with known human toxicity outputs ( Table 3 ).",
      "topic": "Assay Performance"
    },
    {
      "quote": "However, we observed high specificity, since no false positives have been detected.",
      "topic": "Neurotoxicity Specificity"
    },

      "quote": "On the other hand, better sensitivity is indeed required because five compounds known to produce some kind of neurotoxicity in humans did not alter larvae locomotion significantly.",
      "topic": "Neurotoxicity Sensitivity"
    },

      "quote": "All in all, the predictive power of zebrafish hepatotoxicity assessment, may be greater than most in silico or in vitro approaches that are traditionally used [ 73 ].",
